title: Peking Duck

seo.title: Peking Duck Recipe: Authentic Crispy Chinese Dinner
seo.metaDescription: Master the art of making authentic Peking Duck at home with our step-by-step recipe. Get crispy skin and tender meat for a perfect Chinese dinner.

seo.imageAlt: A whole roasted Peking Duck with crispy skin, ready to be carved and served with pancakes and hoisin sauce.
seo.imageCaption: Achieve perfectly crispy skin and tender meat with our authentic Peking Duck recipe, a show-stopping Chinese dinner.

description: Peking Duck is a legendary Chinese delicacy celebrated for its incredibly crispy skin and succulent, tender meat. This iconic dish involves a meticulous preparation process that yields a glistening, mahogany-colored bird. Served traditionally with thin pancakes, hoisin sauce, and fresh scallions, it offers an unforgettable culinary experience.

ingredients.notes: fresh or thawed, neck and giblets removed

instructions.title: Prepare the Duck
instructions.text: Rinse the duck thoroughly inside and out. Pat dry with paper towels. Trim excess fat from the cavity. Using a small pump or syringe, if available, gently inflate the duck under the skin to separate it from the meat (optional but traditional). Pour boiling water over the duck skin evenly until it tightens. Pat dry again.

instructions.title: Apply the Glaze & Air Dry
instructions.text: In a bowl, whisk together maltose syrup, Shaoxing wine, rice vinegar, dark soy sauce, and five-spice powder. Generously brush the glaze all over the duck. Hang the duck in a cool, airy place or on a rack in the refrigerator, uncovered, for at least 12-24 hours to air dry completely. This step is crucial for crispy skin.

instructions.title: Preheat Oven & Prepare for Roasting
instructions.text: Preheat your oven to 375F (190C). Place the duck on a rack set over a roasting pan filled with about 1 inch of water (this helps keep the duck moist and prevents smoking).

instructions.title: Initial Roast
instructions.text: Roast the duck for 30 minutes at 375F (190C). This initial high heat helps crisp the skin.

instructions.title: Continue Roasting
instructions.text: After 30 minutes, reduce the oven temperature to 325F (160C). Continue roasting for another 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes, or until the internal temperature of the duck thigh reaches 180F (82C) and the skin is deep golden brown and crispy. If the skin is browning too quickly, loosely tent it with foil.

instructions.title: Rest and Carve
instructions.text: Remove the duck from the oven and let it rest for 15-20 minutes before carving. This allows the juices to redistribute and makes carving easier. While resting, warm the Mandarin pancakes and prepare the julienned cucumber and scallions. Carve the crispy skin and tender meat into thin slices.

instructions.title: Assemble and Enjoy
instructions.text: Serve the carved duck immediately with warm pancakes, hoisin sauce, cucumber, and scallions. Guests can assemble their own wraps by spreading hoisin on a pancake, adding duck, cucumber, and scallions, then rolling it up.

tips: The drying process is absolutely critical for achieving the signature crispy skin of Peking Duck. Do not skip or rush this step; overnight drying in the fridge is ideal.
For a deeper color and flavor in the glaze, ensure you are using maltose syrup if possible. If unavailable, honey mixed with a touch of dark soy sauce can be a suitable substitute.
Always serve Peking Duck immediately after carving with warm pancakes, fresh scallions, and cucumber juliennes. The combination of textures and flavors is what makes this dish so special.
